reason: E2 directly supports low-temperature HEA synthesis on TiO2 via hydrogen spillover, but the resulting particles are nanoparticles, not sub-nanometric clusters. E1 demonstrates sub-nanometric HEA clusters via spillover on CeO2, not TiO2, and under NO reduction, not full exhaust conditions. The extrapolation to sub-nanometric clusters on TiO2 and to complex exhaust mixtures with H2O and transient operation is not directly evidenced.
premises: Hydrogen spillover on TiO2 enables simultaneous reduction of multiple metal precursors at low temperature (~400 °C)
Simultaneous reduction yields sub-nanometric, highly dispersed HEA clusters with intimate mixing
Sub-nanometric HEA clusters resist sintering and elemental segregation
Such clusters exhibit enhanced low-temperature catalytic activity and durability
The synthesis and performance are applicable to automotive exhaust conditions (H2O, NO, transient operation)
